newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African money market shortage falls Fri, Sat.
newsitem.headline: S.African money market shortage falls Fri, Sat.

text.p: South Africa's money market shortage fell back sharply on Friday and Saturday, after nudging 9.7 billion rand on Thursday, easing pressure for an immediate interest rate hike.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 8.81 billion rand on Friday and 8.74 billion on Saturday.

The shortage had kicked up to 9.69 billion on Thursday from 8.667 billion on Wednesday -- a sharp rise which dealers attributed to month-end pressures and an outflow of funds following the rand's tumble last week.

On the money market, three-month NCD rates were fractionally higher at between 16.40 and 16.50 percent offered from 16.35 to 16.50 percent previously, while the 90-day BA rate was also slightly firmer at between 15.85 and 15.75 percent from 15.85 to 15.70.

Thursday's high money market shortage had fuelled speculation on Friday that the central Reserve Bank would announce an interest rate hike over the weekend or that the authorities were set to announce the abolition of some of the country's remaining exchange controls.
In the event, there was no announcement.
